title: Trapping Rain Water
statement:
Given `n` non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is `1`, compute how much water it can trap after raining.

Water trapped above index `i` is bounded by `min(maxLeft(i), maxRight(i)) - height[i]`, where `maxLeft`/`maxRight` are the tallest bars to the left/right of `i` (inclusive). Two pointers moving inward from both ends can track these running maxes in a single O(n) pass without extra arrays.

examples.explanation: The elevation map traps 6 units of water between the bars.

editorial.approach: Use two pointers, `left = 0` and `right = n - 1`, and track `leftMax`/`rightMax` seen so far. At each step, compare `height[left]` and `height[right]`. If `height[left] < height[right]`, the water trapped at `left` is bounded by `leftMax` (since a taller bar exists somewhere to the right), so update `leftMax` and add `leftMax - height[left]` to the total, then advance `left`. Otherwise, do the symmetric operation on the right side. This avoids the O(n) extra space of precomputing left-max and right-max arrays.
